To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tracking of physical activity in different physical activity settings was low in a representative longitudinal sample of German adolescents and young adults.
tracking of physical activity in different domains from adolescence into adulthood in a representative population is low and that tracking differs by domain.

physical activity indices showed low stability over time, but significant changes were observed for leisure-time physical activity (outside sports clubs), sports club physical activities and overall physical activity, while no changes were observed for overall sports index.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the tracking of physical activity and the determinants of physical activity in different age groups and settings.
a better understanding of tracking of physical activity and its determinants in order to develop effective interventions for the promotion of physical activity.
the question of how to promote physical activity in children and adolescents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the current study are consistent with the existing literature and that physical activity is not stable.
tracking is a complex process and the results are inconsistent.
physical activity tracking in adolescence and young adulthood is low.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tracking of physical activity in adolescence and early adulthood is not a stable phenomenon.
physical activity in different setting is a fluctuating behaviour.
the results of the study are comparable to previous studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
physical activity is not a stable trait and should be measured repeatedly over a long period of time to assess the impact on health.
tracking coefficients are not a good predictor of change in physical activity.
physical activity is not a stable variable and that interventions should focus on the whole life course.
